AccountLinkCreateRequest.description:
Link one outside identity to one member (organiser act).

``external_user_id`` is the speaker's id in the outside
system — the key. ``external_name`` is the name that
system showed for them: evidence for the human making
the link, never a matching key.
AccountLinkCreateRequest.title: AccountLinkCreateRequest

AgendaResponse.description: One agenda page: occurrences + the next page's cursor.
AgendaResponse.title: AgendaResponse

AltTextUpdateRequest.description:
A person's own description of a flyer (B-065): the human
road to alt_text_status "complete". The words are stored as
given (whitespace tidied); an empty or placeholder text is
refused by the service — it would not be a description.
AltTextUpdateRequest.title: AltTextUpdateRequest

AnnouncementChangeView.description:
One line of a re-announce draft (B-078), in the humanised
words the draft itself carries.
AnnouncementChangeView.title: AnnouncementChangeView

AnnouncementCreateRequest.description:
Post to the board. Times arrive as ISO-8601; the router
converts them to stored UTC before the service runs.
AnnouncementCreateRequest.title: AnnouncementCreateRequest

AnnouncementDraftResponse.description:
A drafted re-announcement (B-078): the body names old →
new for every material change it covers. ``sent_at`` /
``sent_by`` record the approval that sent it as change
alerts (Phase 8, B-097); null until then.
AnnouncementDraftResponse.title: AnnouncementDraftResponse

AnnouncementPatchRequest.description:
Edit a post; only sent fields change. An explicit
``expires_at: null`` un-expires the post.
AnnouncementPatchRequest.title: AnnouncementPatchRequest

AnnouncementResponse.description:
One board post. ``expired`` is computed at read time —
expiry is a state the row grows into, never a deletion.
AnnouncementResponse.title: AnnouncementResponse

ApiKeyCreateRequest.description: Mint an API key with chosen scopes (B-014).
ApiKeyCreateRequest.title: ApiKeyCreateRequest

ApiKeyResponse.description:
One API key as listed. ``key`` is present ONLY in the create
response — the one moment the full key is ever shown.
ApiKeyResponse.title: ApiKeyResponse

ApplyWinnerRequest.description:
Mint path only: the new event's title (defaults to the
poll's question).
ApplyWinnerRequest.title: ApplyWinnerRequest

AskRequest.description: A member's question to the group's approved history.
AskRequest.title: AskRequest

AskResponse.description:
The ask answer (B-115). ``verified`` False means
``answer`` IS the honest refusal — its first words are
"I couldn't verify this" — and its citations are labelled
unverified by their null chunk ids.
AskResponse.title: AskResponse

AttendanceEventSummary.description:
One recent event in the planning summary: the event and
its headcount. No people.
AttendanceEventSummary.title: AttendanceEventSummary

AttendanceMarkRequest.description: Mark one member present at the event in the path.
AttendanceMarkRequest.title: AttendanceMarkRequest

AttendanceMarkResponse.description:
The mark's own receipt — the ONLY response in this area
that names a person, because it echoes the organiser's act
itself. There is no list shape beside it, deliberately.
AttendanceMarkResponse.title: AttendanceMarkResponse

AttendanceSummaryResponse.description:
"Last three club nights drew ~20", as data: recent
events, their headcounts, and the average.
AttendanceSummaryResponse.title: AttendanceSummaryResponse

AvailabilitySlotResponse.description:
One proposed slot with its marks and its rank inputs —
can/can't counts and who said which (the group's own marks,
nothing else; B-090's privacy boundary is this shape).
AvailabilitySlotResponse.title: AvailabilitySlotResponse

BriefingResponse.description:
A host briefing (B-117): the woven text, the questions
the history leaves open (the model's list), and the role
gaps (the data's list — unclaimed slots, counted, not
imagined).
BriefingResponse.title: BriefingResponse

CancelRequest.description: Cancellation carries the reason in the canceller's words.
CancelRequest.title: CancelRequest

CandidateCreateRequest.description: Draft a candidate for the review queue (stub, B-018).
CandidateCreateRequest.title: CandidateCreateRequest

CandidateDetailResponse.description: The full candidate: the list row plus provenance rows.
CandidateDetailResponse.title: CandidateDetailResponse

CandidateEditRequest.description:
A reviewer's edit of the draft (organiser+). The draft is
the same JSON shape the pipeline wrote; the reviewer replaces
field values, and the API recomputes flags afterwards (B-044
— flags are the API's to decide, never the client's).
CandidateEditRequest.title: CandidateEditRequest

CandidateMergeRequest.description: Merge this candidate INTO the named survivor.
CandidateMergeRequest.title: CandidateMergeRequest

CandidateResponse.description:
A candidate as the queue shows it.

Grown in Phase 3 (B-043) with the review queue's triage data —
draft, confidence, server-computed flags (B-044), prompt
provenance (B-038) — all additive: the B-018 stub fields are
unchanged. ``resulting_entity_*`` stay null until Phase 4
mints published entities; approval records the decision.
CandidateResponse.title: CandidateResponse

ChunkIn.description: One chunk of content handed to the sources core.
ChunkIn.title: ChunkIn

ChunkResponse.description: One chunk as read back, in source order.
ChunkResponse.title: ChunkResponse

CitationResponse.description:
One claim's receipt. ``chunk_id``/``position`` are null
only on an unverified answer, where the quote is shown as
found material, never as proof.
CitationResponse.title: CitationResponse

CommentResponse.description:
One comment as a viewer at some level sees it: hidden and
deleted are organiser-visible flags; to members a hidden or
deleted comment is simply absent from the list (the service
filters it before this shape is built).

The parent is named honestly since B-084 generalised the
thread system: ``parent_type`` + ``parent_id`` always;
``event_id`` remains, populated for event parents (the
B-060 shape), null for task/decision/poll parents.
CommentResponse.title: CommentResponse

resource_note.default: Resource double-bookings appear above as resource_overlap flags when two published events hold the same resource over overlapping times.
resource_note.title: Resource Note

ContradictionResponse.description:
A disagreement an event carries (B-079) — visible until
a person resolves it; resolved rows keep who chose and
what they chose.
ContradictionResponse.title: ContradictionResponse

ContradictionValueView.description:
One side of a contradiction (B-079): the value (in the
change-history string form), the sources that said it, and
whether it is the value the event currently carries.
ContradictionValueView.title: ContradictionValueView

CostLineCreateRequest.description:
``amount_cents`` is an int — a float body is refused by
this schema before any service runs (B-089's law).
CostLineCreateRequest.title: CostLineCreateRequest

DigestResponse.description: A stored digest (B-099): both renderings, as sent.
DigestResponse.title: DigestResponse

DriftEntryResponse.description:
One drifted outside copy: which event, which door, and
how it drifted — "differs" (edited outside) or "missing"
(deleted outside). Reconciliation reports; it never
repairs.
DriftEntryResponse.title: DriftEntryResponse

EmailChangeRequest.description:
Ask to move the account to a new email (B-020). The change
completes only when the token sent to the NEW address is used.
EmailChangeRequest.title: EmailChangeRequest

EmailInRequest.description:
One delivered email, in the webhook shape providers share
(B-030). The real provider adapter lands in Phase 12.
EmailInRequest.title: EmailInRequest

EmbedOriginsRequest.description:
Replace a group's embed register whole (admin act):
the web origins allowed to embed its public page. An
origin is a scheme + host — never a path.
EmbedOriginsRequest.title: EmbedOriginsRequest

EraseRequest.description:
The double confirmation (B-143): the group's EXACT
name, typed back, and the word ERASE. Anything less is a
422 and the group stands untouched — a destructive act
must be impossible to perform by accident or by a stray
client retry with a stale body.
EraseRequest.title: EraseRequest

EraseResponse.description:
What an erasure reports: the fact, the per-table row
counts that were destroyed, and how many stored files went
with them. Never any content — the content is gone, and
the receipt must not become a copy of it.
EraseResponse.title: EraseResponse

EventAttendanceResponse.description: One event's attendance, as a count and nothing else.
EventAttendanceResponse.title: EventAttendanceResponse

EventChangeResponse.description: One row of an event's change history (B-050).
EventChangeResponse.title: EventChangeResponse

EventCreateRequest.description:
Direct organiser entry (B-049). Times are ISO-8601; the
router converts them to stored UTC before the service runs.
EventCreateRequest.title: EventCreateRequest

EventPatchRequest.description:
An event edit (B-050). Every field optional; the router
passes only the fields actually sent (exclude_unset) — an
absent field is untouched, an explicit value is a change.
EventPatchRequest.title: EventPatchRequest

EventResponse.description:
One event at one projection level (B-059). Fields above a
level's line are simply absent (None / default) below it.
EventResponse.title: EventResponse

EventSourceLinkResponse.description:
One supporting source of an event, with its quote
(B-076's answerable provenance): "where did this field
come from?" is this list.
EventSourceLinkResponse.title: EventSourceLinkResponse

ExceptionRequest.description:
One per-occurrence override: this happening moved, or is
cancelled where it stood. Times are LOCAL ISO in the event's
timezone (the wall clock the group thinks in).
ExceptionRequest.title: ExceptionRequest

ExtractAcceptedResponse.description: 202: the run is a job; poll the job or watch the stream.
ExtractAcceptedResponse.title: ExtractAcceptedResponse

ExtractRequest.description:
Ask for an extraction run over one source (B-045). Kinds
default to all four; a subset re-runs just those kinds.
ExtractRequest.title: ExtractRequest

FacebookDraftResponse.description:
The draft as the organiser receives it: Meta-shaped
payload, a copy-ready text block, and the cover suggestion.
FacebookDraftResponse.title: FacebookDraftResponse

FacebookPublishResponse.description:
Where one event stands on Facebook (B-131): its copy's
state, the outside id and URL once created, whether the
copy still matches the event here — and, on a press, what
the press did.
FacebookPublishResponse.title: FacebookPublishResponse

FeedIssueRequest.description:
Issue a feed, optionally narrowed: statuses (published /
cancelled), a place word, a sub-group. The filter is part of
the issued feed — a leaked URL leaks only its own scope.
FeedIssueRequest.title: FeedIssueRequest

FeedIssueResponse.description:
The issuing response — the ONE time the raw token and its
ready-to-paste URLs exist (B-053).
FeedIssueResponse.title: FeedIssueResponse

FeedResponse.description: A feed as its group sees it: prefix only, never the token.
FeedResponse.title: FeedResponse

FlyerResponse.description:
An image source's picture record (B-027/B-028).

``alt_text_status`` is the visible-defect flag: it reads
``awaiting_description`` — and ``alt_text`` is the literal
placeholder — until a real description of the image exists
(Phase 5: the vision pass's drafted description, or a
person's own words via the flyer PATCH).
FlyerResponse.title: FlyerResponse

FlyerView.description:
A flyer's public face on an event: the picture and its
description state. An undescribed flyer says so — the alt
text law (B-065) makes the defect visible, never silent. A
generated image says so too (B-067): ``generated`` rides
every projection because it is a column on the flyer, not a
label a projection could forget.
FlyerView.title: FlyerView

FlyerWallEntry.description:
One poster on the wall: the picture record, its reading
state, and its event when approval has made one.

``review_status`` is the honest one-word state: the event's
own status when an event exists, else ``pending_review`` — a
poster nobody has approved yet is ON the wall, labelled,
never invisible (B-070). A poster whose reading failed says
``read_failed`` (B-069's partial truth, on the wall too).
FlyerWallEntry.title: FlyerWallEntry

GapsResponse.description:
"What is still missing?" for one event (B-086): one flat
gaps list (badge-shaped) plus the sections behind it.
GapsResponse.title: GapsResponse

GenerateImageRequest.description:
Ask for a generated event image (B-067). ``description``
is the organiser's own words for the picture — they steer
the generation and, when they are a genuine description,
become its alt text (B-065's human road).
GenerateImageRequest.title: GenerateImageRequest

GooglePullResponse.description:
One Google inbound pull's counts (B-159): how many
Google-side edits were drafted as change candidates, out
of how many linked copies were compared.
GooglePullResponse.title: GooglePullResponse

GoogleSyncResponse.description:
One Google sync run's counts: copies created, copies
brought back into agreement, cancellations propagated,
and copies already current (left alone).
GoogleSyncResponse.title: GoogleSyncResponse

GroupCreateRequest.description: Create a group; the creator becomes its owner (B-015).
GroupCreateRequest.title: GroupCreateRequest

GroupResponse.description: A group as the API shows it.
GroupResponse.title: GroupResponse

GroupSettingsResponse.description:
The settings pack as read (B-111): the review-queue
rules, reminder defaults, the digest's moment, the
template set, and the AI budget cap (null = no cap).
GroupSettingsResponse.title: GroupSettingsResponse

GroupSettingsUpdateRequest.description:
A settings-pack write. Every field is optional: a field
that is ABSENT is left as it was; a field that is present
governs — including null where null means something
(budget → no cap; digest weekday → the default).
GroupSettingsUpdateRequest.title: GroupSettingsUpdateRequest

HealthBoardEntryResponse.description:
One integration on the health board: its recorded
verdict and the single next step, in words.
HealthBoardEntryResponse.title: HealthBoardEntryResponse

HealthResponse.description:
The first thing to check when "it doesn't work" (roadmap §5).

``checks`` is the deepened view (B-155): database engine,
job-queue shape, configured drivers, and the storage
probe — the numbers RUNBOOK.md's five failures key on.
HealthResponse.title: HealthResponse

ImportRowIssue.description:
One row of the spreadsheet, named by its row number,
with the plain reason it was skipped or failed (B-110).
ImportRowIssue.title: ImportRowIssue

InboundAddressResponse.description:
A group's email-in channel (B-030).

``token`` and ``address`` appear ONLY in the creation
response — the one time the secret exists outside the hash.
InboundAddressResponse.title: InboundAddressResponse

InstantiationResponse.description:
What instantiating built: the event (full event view
rides in ``event`` as a plain dict from the events schema)
and the ids of the plan built around it.
InstantiationResponse.title: InstantiationResponse

IntegrationCreateRequest.description:
Register one integration (admin act).

``config`` is the connector's settings as a JSON object —
tokens and keys inside it are sealed before they touch
the database and are never read back out through the API
(responses carry only the NAMES of the config keys).
IntegrationCreateRequest.title: IntegrationCreateRequest

IntegrationUpdateRequest.description:
Replace an integration's name and/or config (admin act).

A present ``config`` replaces the sealed config whole —
partial secret updates are how stale half-rotated keys
happen, so the framework does not offer them.
IntegrationUpdateRequest.title: IntegrationUpdateRequest

InviteCreateRequest.description: Invite one address to one event (B-098).
InviteCreateRequest.title: InviteCreateRequest

InviteRequest.description: Invite a person by email with a starting role (B-016).
InviteRequest.title: InviteRequest

InviteRespondRequest.description: Answer an invite without an account (B-098).
InviteRespondRequest.title: InviteRespondRequest

InviteRespondResponse.description:
The answer's record: attributed to the invited address,
with the account offer stated, never hidden.
InviteRespondResponse.title: InviteRespondResponse

InviteResponse.description:
An invite as its creator sees it. ``link`` carries the
raw token and is present ONLY on the creation response —
the token is shown once (B-014's discipline); later reads
show the prefix only.
InviteResponse.title: InviteResponse

JobResponse.description: A job's state as its enqueuer can poll it (B-008).
JobResponse.title: JobResponse

LinkIngestRequest.description: Paste a link to be fetched and archived (B-029).
LinkIngestRequest.title: LinkIngestRequest

LiveSourceRequest.description:
Register a live-chat source (B-032): connector, the
conversation's id there, and — never optional — the scope
the granting member gave.
LiveSourceRequest.title: LiveSourceRequest

LiveSyncResponse.description: The result of one poll of a live source (B-123).
LiveSyncResponse.title: LiveSyncResponse

MagicLinkRequest.description: Ask for a sign-in link by email (B-012).
MagicLinkRequest.title: MagicLinkRequest

MailWebhookRequest.description:
A provider's delivery webhook, stubbed shape (B-102):
the provider signs and authenticates with its own driver
in Phase 12; the recorded shape is this.
MailWebhookRequest.title: MailWebhookRequest

MatchView.description:
One scored match of this candidate against an existing
event (B-075): the event's face, the total score, the
per-component scores (title / time / place / host), and the
``likely`` verdict — at or above the threshold the queue
shows "likely the same event" beside the merge action.
MatchView.title: MatchView

MeDataResponse.description:
Everything the system holds about the caller (B-144),
in sections named the way a person would name them. The
leaves are plain records; the service guarantees no hash
or secret appears anywhere in them.
MeDataResponse.title: MeDataResponse

MemberExportRow.description:
One exported membership: the roster row, with the
person's sub-group names (B-110).
MemberExportRow.title: MemberExportRow

MemberImportReportResponse.description:
What an import did — or, on a dry run, exactly what it
WOULD do (the report is computed, then rolled back).
MemberImportReportResponse.title: MemberImportReportResponse

MembershipResponse.description: One membership row: who, with which role, in which state.
MembershipResponse.title: MembershipResponse

MergeEventRequest.description:
Merge this candidate into the named existing EVENT
(B-076): the field-level merge — better-sourced values
win, provenance becomes the event's links.
MergeEventRequest.title: MergeEventRequest

MergeEventResponse.description:
What a merge did, field by field (B-076): the event as
it now stands, which fields were filled / applied (won) /
agreed without moving / kept (the event's value stood),
which were skipped as unsupported or unresolved, and the
contradictions the merge opened (B-079).
MergeEventResponse.title: MergeEventResponse

MetaResponse.description: Public facts about this deployment: name, version, contract.
MetaResponse.title: MetaResponse

MissingRole.description: One role an event still needs people for.
MissingRole.title: MissingRole

NewsletterDraftRequest.description:
The month whose approved recaps become a newsletter
draft (B-118).
NewsletterDraftRequest.title: NewsletterDraftRequest

NotificationResponse.description: One notification: one row, both channels, full state.
NotificationResponse.title: NotificationResponse

OccurrenceResponse.description:
One concrete happening (B-052/B-055): the event's identity
fields plus THIS occurrence's times — rendered in the event's
timezone with true offsets, UTC alongside. A frontend never
expands a rule itself.
OccurrenceResponse.title: OccurrenceResponse

PasswordChangeRequest.description: Set a new password, proving the current one (B-020).
PasswordChangeRequest.title: PasswordChangeRequest

PasteIngestRequest.description: Paste a chat export or plain text as a source (B-024).
PasteIngestRequest.title: PasteIngestRequest

PlanningDigestResponse.description:
"State of the plan" (B-093): the week's events, what is
unclaimed, what is unanswered, what is undecided.
PlanningDigestResponse.title: PlanningDigestResponse

PollResultsResponse.description:
The tally as answered AFTER the vote commits (B-087):
every option's count, the total, and the leader(s) — a tie
returns two leaders and says so by shape.
PollResultsResponse.title: PollResultsResponse

PreferencesResponse.description: The member's full effective policy in one group.
PreferencesResponse.title: PreferencesResponse

PreferencesUpdateRequest.description:
Write switches and/or quiet hours. ``quiet_hours``
omitted leaves them untouched; an explicit empty object
clears them (the service owns that reading).
PreferencesUpdateRequest.title: PreferencesUpdateRequest

PrintEventRow.description:
One event as the noticeboard needs it: every fact present
as text (B-072). ``when`` is words ("Saturday 24 October
2026, 7:00 PM – 9:00 PM"), not an instant — paper has no
timezone conversions.
PrintEventRow.title: PrintEventRow

PrintMonthResponse.description:
A month's print listing (B-072): the structured rows plus
the whole listing as one plain-text document the frontend
can hand to a printer as-is.
PrintMonthResponse.title: PrintMonthResponse

ProvenanceEntry.description:
One field's evidence: the quote, its chunk, and whether the
pipeline verified it (an unsupported field is shown, never
hidden — that is the queue's whole point). For a picture's
fields the evidence is a REGION instead (B-063): the box
[x, y, w, h] the field was read from, so the queue can
highlight the rectangle on the poster.
ProvenanceEntry.title: ProvenanceEntry

PruneRunResponse.description:
One pruning run's full account (B-120): input, kept,
dropped, passes, model, cost — dropping is visible.
PruneRunResponse.title: PruneRunResponse

PublicInviteResponse.description:
An invite's public face: the event, and whether an
account is on offer (it always is, after answering).
PublicInviteResponse.title: PublicInviteResponse

PublicPageResponse.description:
The public page payload (B-135): a public-listed
group's face for its own website and for embeds — the
group's public facts and its events at the PUBLIC
projection (B-059). Nothing member-only exists here.
PublicPageResponse.title: PublicPageResponse

QuestionResolveRequest.description:
Resolve, optionally minting the answer as a decision in
the same call (B-086).
QuestionResolveRequest.title: QuestionResolveRequest

QueueStatusResponse.description:
The queue's plain-words state (B-047): how much waits, and
— when the group's daily AI budget is spent — that extraction
is "paused — budget", said exactly that plainly.
QueueStatusResponse.title: QueueStatusResponse

QuietHours.description: The member's quiet window (B-100), in their timezone.
QuietHours.title: QuietHours

RecapResponse.description:
A recap draft (B-118) — a draft, always: it becomes
memory only through approval.
RecapResponse.title: RecapResponse

RecurrenceRequest.description:
Set/replace a series rule (B-052). ``exceptions`` replaces
the whole exception list; omit it to keep the existing ones.
RecurrenceRequest.title: RecurrenceRequest

RecurrenceResponse.description: A series rule as stored, with its exceptions (B-052).
RecurrenceResponse.title: RecurrenceResponse

RefreshRequest.description: Exchange a refresh token for a fresh session (B-013).
RefreshRequest.title: RefreshRequest

RegisterRequest.description: Create an account with email + password (B-011).
RegisterRequest.title: RegisterRequest

ReminderRule.description:
One reminder rule (B-096): N days before, or the
morning of. Days is required (1..365) for days_before and
ignored for morning_of.
ReminderRule.title: ReminderRule

ResolveContradictionRequest.description:
Settle a contradiction (B-079): the chosen value must be
one the sources actually said (the service checks); ``note``
rides into the change history as the reason.
ResolveContradictionRequest.title: ResolveContradictionRequest

ResourceBookingCreateRequest.description: Book one resource for the event in the path.
ResourceBookingCreateRequest.title: ResourceBookingCreateRequest

ResourceBookingResponse.description:
One booking. ``conflicts`` carries the double-bookings
this booking takes part in — the booker sees the clash in
the response that makes it (flags, never blocks).
ResourceBookingResponse.title: ResourceBookingResponse

ResourceConflictFlag.description:
One double-booking a booking takes part in (B-057's
shape, on the booking that created it).
ResourceConflictFlag.title: ResourceConflictFlag

ResourceCreateRequest.description:
Register a bookable item, with its keeper: a member's id
(their words become the label), or plain words.
ResourceCreateRequest.title: ResourceCreateRequest

ResourcePatchRequest.description: Edit an item; only sent fields change.
ResourcePatchRequest.title: ResourcePatchRequest

ResourceResponse.description: One bookable item and its keeper.
ResourceResponse.title: ResourceResponse

RetentionRunResponse.description: A retention sweep's receipt: counts only (B-144).
RetentionRunResponse.title: RetentionRunResponse

RsvpListResponse.description: Every answer plus the summary counts (B-061).
RsvpListResponse.title: RsvpListResponse

RsvpRequest.description:
The caller's own answer (B-061): an upsert — answering
again updates the same row, it never stacks a second one.
RsvpRequest.title: RsvpRequest

SamtalCalendarSyncResponse.description:
One run of the Samtal calendar return path (B-124):
how many events were pushed out, and how many Samtal-side
edits arrived as change candidates for the queue.
SamtalCalendarSyncResponse.title: SamtalCalendarSyncResponse

SeatCreateRequest.description:
Create an agent seat (B-018): a name, a role, and the scopes
its key will carry. Approval is never among a seat's powers.
SeatCreateRequest.title: SeatCreateRequest

SeatResponse.description: A seat as listed. ``key`` appears only at creation.
SeatResponse.title: SeatResponse

SessionResponse.description:
What a successful sign-in returns: short-lived access token,
rotating refresh token, and who it belongs to.
SessionResponse.title: SessionResponse

ShiftCreateRequest.description:
Open a shift on an event: one role, one window, a
headcount. Times arrive as ISO-8601; the router converts
them to stored UTC before the service runs.
ShiftCreateRequest.title: ShiftCreateRequest

ShiftGapReportResponse.description: The window's gap report: only events WITH gaps appear.
ShiftGapReportResponse.title: ShiftGapReportResponse

ShiftGapResponse.description:
One event's gaps, with the summary in words a coordinator
can read aloud: "Saturday still needs a driver and a door
person."
ShiftGapResponse.title: ShiftGapResponse

ShiftResponse.description:
One shift: the role, the window, how many people it
needs, how many have claimed — and the slot rows themselves
(claims and releases ride the B-088 slot endpoints).
ShiftResponse.title: ShiftResponse

SourceCreateRequest.description: Create a text-native source with its chunks (B-023).
SourceCreateRequest.title: SourceCreateRequest

SourceDetailResponse.description: A source with its chunks, in order (B-023).
SourceDetailResponse.title: SourceDetailResponse

SourcePermissionEntry.description:
One source's permission record, in plain words (B-144):
what it is, who added it, and the permission they recorded
when they did — the words the group can audit.
SourcePermissionEntry.title: SourcePermissionEntry

SourceResponse.description: A source as lists show it: the container + permission record.
SourceResponse.title: SourceResponse

SpeakerResponse.description:
One speaker in a live source, resolved (B-123).

``guest`` is True exactly when no account link resolves
this speaker — including when their display name matches
a member's name letter for letter. That is the identity
law, rendered.
SpeakerResponse.title: SpeakerResponse

SubGroupCreateRequest.description: Open a named sub-group (a chapter, a crew) in a group.
SubGroupCreateRequest.title: SubGroupCreateRequest

SubGroupEnrollRequest.description:
Enrol one group member; ``role`` is the optional
per-sub-group role override (an organiser's grant).
SubGroupEnrollRequest.title: SubGroupEnrollRequest

SubGroupMemberResponse.description:
One enrolled member: their group role, their per-sub-group
role when one was granted, and the effective role.
SubGroupMemberResponse.title: SubGroupMemberResponse

SubGroupPatchRequest.description: Rename / re-describe a sub-group; only sent fields change.
SubGroupPatchRequest.title: SubGroupPatchRequest

SubGroupResponse.description: One sub-group, with its enrolled headcount.
SubGroupResponse.title: SubGroupResponse

SummariseRequest.description:
Which thread to summarise (B-116): the discussion
parents the thread system knows (B-084).
SummariseRequest.title: SummariseRequest

SummariseResponse.description:
A discussion summary and the candidates it proposed
(B-116): the summary is a draft; the candidates wait in the
review queue — the queue disposes.
SummariseResponse.title: SummariseResponse

SummaryResponse.description: One thing the memory engine said, with its receipts.
SummaryResponse.title: SummaryResponse

SupplyLineResponse.description: One folded shopping line of the merged view (B-088).
SupplyLineResponse.title: SupplyLineResponse

TaskCreateRequest.description:
Direct human entry. Naming ``owner_id`` here IS the
assignment — a person's act, validated against membership
in the service.
TaskCreateRequest.title: TaskCreateRequest

TokenConsumeRequest.description: Present a one-time token (magic link / reset / email change).
TokenConsumeRequest.title: TokenConsumeRequest

UserResponse.description: A person's public profile. Never carries any credential.
UserResponse.title: UserResponse

VisionReadAcceptedResponse.description:

public page.

The queue: newest first, filterable by kind, status, and

schema.title: Response List Candidates Api V1 Groups  Group Id  Candidates Get

Draft a candidate. Needs membership (member+) AND, for key

get.description:
How much waits + the budget truth, in plain words (B-047):

and ``pause_reason`` is "budget" — the queue says

One candidate with its full provenance (B-043): every

patch.description:
Edit a draft (organiser+). Status becomes "edited"; flags
are recomputed by the API, never taken from the client.

post.description:
Approve a candidate (a person with publish rights).

The door is membership: WHO may approve is the group's own
review rule (settings pack, B-111), enforced inside the
service beside B-018's seat rule — a group may open
approval to members or hold it to admins, and may require
more than one distinct approver before a candidate is
decided; below the count this records the approval and the
candidate stays pending.

Merge this candidate into the named survivor (organiser+).
Returns the survivor; the merged row keeps its draft and
provenance under its new status.

Merge this candidate into an existing event (B-076):
the field-level merge — better-sourced values win, all
sources link to the event, and a genuine disagreement the
merge cannot settle becomes a contradiction on the event
(B-079). This is the merge action beside the queue's
"likely the same event" proposal (B-075).

Reject a draft (organiser+). The draft and its provenance
stay — rejection is a decision, not an erasure.
Promise this line yourself.
Release a line you claimed.

delete.description: Delete your own comment: a tombstone, returned flagged.

patch.description: Edit your own comment (nobody else's — ever).

Conflict flags over a window (B-057): double-booked

blocks — reading them changes nothing.

The decisions log, newest first. ``?current=true`` is

schema.title: Response List Decisions Api V1 Groups  Group Id  Decisions Get

Record a decision, optionally superseding an earlier

Compose and send this week's digest now (organiser+),

schema.title: Response List Digests Api V1 Groups  Group Id  Digests Get

post.description:
Hard-erase the group (B-143). Double confirmation: the
group's exact name typed back, and the word ERASE. A
mismatch refuses with the group untouched.

get.description:
The group's events, soonest first, at the caller's
projection level. Drafts appear only for organisers, and
sub-group-scoped events only for their people (B-105).

schema.title: Response List Events Api V1 Groups  Group Id  Events Get

post.description:
Direct organiser entry (B-049): the entry records a manual

delete.description:
Delete an event (organiser+): it vanishes from every
read at once and leaves a 30-day tombstone (B-080).

get.description:
One event. A draft asked for by a non-organiser is a 404 —
the bright line (B-049) is existence-level, not field-level.

patch.description:
Edit an event (B-050, D-15): If-Match carries the version
read; every changed field lands in the change history; the
response carries the new ETag. A capacity change re-runs
the RSVP waitlist (B-061) — a bigger room promotes the line.

get.description:
One event's headcount. A count — there is no per-person
read here, deliberately (B-109's refusal).

post.description:
Mark a member present (organiser+). Idempotent — the
receipt is the act's own echo, not a read of anyone's
record.

delete.description: Correct a mark (organiser+).

post.description:
The host's briefing for one event: past decisions, last
recap, open questions, role gaps — and the pruned history
that matters, landmines included.

get.description:
The balance summary: total + per-member paid totals,
every number exact integer cents (B-089).

post.description:
Cancel with a reason (B-051): the event stays, marked
cancelled everywhere it was ever shown.

get.description: The event's change feed — complete, in order (B-050).

schema.title: Response List Changes Api V1 Groups  Group Id  Events  Event Id  Changes Get
Response List Checklist Items Api V1 Groups  Group Id  Events  Event Id  Checklist Get

post.description: Add a bring/prepare line to an event's list.

Clone last time's event (B-051): structure copies, RSVPs
and discussion never do; the clone is born a draft.

get.description: An event's discussion thread.

schema.title: Response List Event Comments Api V1 Groups  Group Id  Events  Event Id  Comments Get

post.description: Say something on an event.

get.description:
The disagreements this event carries (B-079): open
ones by default — a visible flag until a person resolves
it; ``include_resolved`` shows the settled history too.

schema.title: Response List Contradictions Api V1 Groups  Group Id  Events  Event Id  Contradictions Get

post.description:
Settle a contradiction (B-079): the chosen value — one
the sources actually said — is applied to the event, and
the resolution is recorded with who chose it.

schema.title: Response List Cost Lines Api V1 Groups  Group Id  Events  Event Id  Costs Get

post.description:
Record one line of what the event cost (integer cents;
the payer defaults to you).

delete.description:
Remove this event's Facebook copy (organiser+): the
reversible half of the press. The event here is
untouched.

get.description:
This event's Facebook standing (organiser+): whether
a copy exists, where it lives, and whether it still
matches the event here.

post.description:
THE PRESS (B-131): create this event on the group's
connected Facebook Page, or bring its copy back into
agreement, or carry its cancellation out.

An outward act, so it happens ONLY here, on an
organiser's explicit call — edits made elsewhere show as
``differs`` until this door is used, and nothing on the
Page side is ever read back into the event. In this
environment the client boundary is the recorded-fixture
double (or the unavailable client): no live Page exists
here, and the press records that honestly.

get.description:
Build the Facebook Event DRAFT for a published event
(B-058). Nothing is created on Facebook — creating the real
event is the Phase 12 integration with a human pressing the
button, because posting as a person/page is an outward act.

"What is still missing?" — missing fields, open
questions, unclaimed roles, unclaimed tasks, in one list.

post.description:
Generate an image for an event that has none (B-067):
stored with ``generated: true`` on its flyer record, so the
flag survives every projection — never passed off as a
photo. An event with a picture already is a 409.

get.description:
One event as a downloadable .ics (B-053). Drafts refuse —
a file download is a publishing-out road, and the bright
line holds for every role here.

An event's invites (prefixes only — the tokens
themselves are gone by design).

schema.title: Response List Invites Api V1 Groups  Group Id  Events  Event Id  Invites Get

post.description:
Invite one address to this event (organiser+). The
response's link is shown ONCE — send it on, or trust the
notification the invitee also receives.

get.description:
This event's occurrences in a window (B-052): the API
returns occurrences, never the rule, so the frontend does
zero date maths. ``from``/``to`` are ISO datetimes; the
default window is the event's start through +92 days.

schema.title: Response List Occurrences Api V1 Groups  Group Id  Events  Event Id  Occurrences Get

post.description: Draft → published (B-049's bright line, crossed on purpose).

get.description: An event's announcement drafts, oldest first (member+).

schema.title: Response List Reannouncement Drafts Api V1 Groups  Group Id  Events  Event Id  Reannounce Drafts Get

Approve a draft and SEND the change alerts (B-097):
exactly the event's RSVP'd people are told, through the
outbox, and the event's needs_reannounce flag clears —
the group has been told.

Draft the event's recap from its discussion, its
attendance count, and its photos' completed alt text.
A draft — it becomes memory only on approval.

delete.description: Remove the rule: the event becomes a one-off (B-052).

The series rule + exceptions for one event (404 when the

in plain words, never discovered later by a reader.

post.description:
Move or cancel ONE occurrence (B-052): the rule stands;
this happening is the exception.

get.description: What an event has booked.

comes back whole — history, links, RSVPs and all.

Withdraw your answer. A freed seat promotes the next in

Download the group's whole archive (B-143): JSON by

get.description:
The period's wall (B-070): every poster in the month —
the ones approval has made events of AND the ones still
waiting, which show as ``pending_review``, never invisible.

patch.description:
Give a flyer a person's own description (B-065) — the
human road to alt-text ``complete``. Words that are not a

Register one integration (admin+). Its config is
sealed before it is stored; the response names the
config keys held and shows no value, ever.

get.description:
The health board (B-136, organiser+): every integration
with its recorded state and ONE next step, in words. This
route is registered BEFORE /{integration_id} on purpose —
"health-board" is a board, not an integration id.

schema.title: Response Integration Health Board Api V1 Groups  Group Id  Integrations Health Board Get

post.description:
Run reconciliation NOW (admin+, B-137): compare the
group's outside copies, notify the organisers of any
drift, return the drift list. Registered before
/{integration_id} routes for the same reason as the
health board. Running it also anchors the nightly chain
if it is not anchored yet.

delete.description: Remove one integration and its sealed config (admin+).

get.description: One integration's record (organiser+).

patch.description:
Rename and/or re-configure one integration (admin+).
A present config replaces the old one whole and resets
the health verdict to unconfigured.

post.description:
Verify a Google Calendar connection's credentials
against the client boundary and record the verdict on
the row (admin+). The sealed token is what a deployment's
OAuth consent flow issued; this door proves it answers
before any sync trusts it.

Pull Google-side edits as CHANGE CANDIDATES (B-159,
organiser+): each edit a person made on the Google copy
is drafted into the review queue — the event does not
move until a person approves the candidate there. Two-way
sync, with the queue never bypassed.

Run one Google Calendar sync (organiser+): published
events upsert into the chosen calendar, cancellations
propagate as cancellations. ONE-WAY OUT — this door never
reads an edit back; the inbound road is google-pull
(B-159), and it drafts candidates, never writes.

Run the health check and record its verdict (admin+):
status, last success, and — when it fails — the error in
plain words, on the record where the list shows it.
Invite a person by email (organiser+).
Accept my invitation to this group.
Decline my invitation to this group.
Leave the group myself (the last owner may not — B-016).

The roster out (admin+): JSON by default, or

The answer is a report — what was created, counted,

``?dry_run=true`` the same report is computed and the work
rolled back: what WOULD happen, truthfully.

patch.description:
Change a member's role (admin+; owner/admin moves are

Every prune/ask/brief run, with kept and dropped chunk

delete.description:
Delete one run record. Summaries are never deleted

get.description:
The month grid (B-055): whole weeks, days marked
in/out of month, occurrences already placed.

post.description:
Weave a month's approved recaps into a newsletter
draft. Drafts only.

get.description:
Failed and dead notifications for this group, with the

post.description:

person's decision, with attempts reset.

get.description: A group's outbound endpoints (organiser+).

get.description:
One endpoint's deliveries, newest first (organiser+):

schema.title: Response List Outbound Deliveries Api V1 Groups  Group Id  Outbound Webhooks  Webhook Id  Deliveries Get

"State of the plan": this week's events, unclaimed

Apply a date poll's winner: move the attached event, or

Freeze the tally (organiser+).

get.description:

post.description:

delete.description: Release one booking (organiser+).

get.description: The group's bookable items, name order.

schema.title: Response List Resources Api V1 Groups  Group Id  Resources Get

post.description: Register a bookable item (organiser+).

delete.description: Remove an item and its bookings (organiser+).

post.description:
Run the group's retention sweep NOW (B-144) — the same
sweep the nightly job runs; the receipt is counts only.
With no window set, the sweep honestly expires nothing.
Take one of the event's named jobs yourself.

get.description:
One search over events, tasks, decisions, questions —
ranked, and every hit linked back to its source. Scoped
hits outside the caller's sub-groups never appear (B-105).
List the group's seats (never their keys).

schema.title: Response List Seats Api V1 Groups  Group Id  Seats Get

post.description: Create an agent seat and receive its key — shown once.

get.description:
The group's settings pack (organiser+): review rules,
reminder defaults, digest moment, template set, AI budget.

put.description:
Write the settings pack (admin+). Only the fields sent
are changed; each is validated whole, the change is
audited with its old and new values, and a digest change
re-anchors the digest chain before the answer is sent.

get.description:
The gap report: which events in the window still need
which roles — "Saturday still needs a driver and a door
person." Without a window, the group's coming week.
Every source in the group, oldest first (member+).

schema.title: Response List Sources Api V1 Groups  Group Id  Sources Get

post.description:
Create a text-native source with its chunks (member+).

The permission record's ``granted_by`` is the caller — filled
here from the principal, never trusted from the request body.

Upload one photo as a flyer (or board) source (member+).

The response's ``flyer`` carries the picture's true upright
dimensions and its alt-text state — which starts, honestly,
as ``awaiting_description``.

Fetch a pasted link and archive its text as a source.

Private, local, and metadata addresses are refused by the
fetch guard (422 ``fetch_blocked``) before a single byte is
requested; a page that cannot be read archives nothing.

Register a live-chat source under a person's grant (B-032).

The registration is the permission record — connector,
conversation, scope, and the granting member — created
before any receiver exists. A seat cannot grant it, and a
scope cannot be empty: services/live.py holds both rules.

Upload one HTML newsletter as a source (member+).

Chunks come back as the newsletter's sections, in order —
twelve events in the email are twelve chunks here.

Paste a chat export or plain text; it is parsed into chunks
by the speaker-line parser (B-024) and stored as one source.

get.description:
Who shared what, on what permission (B-144) — every
source's permission record in plain words, readable by
any member: a group should be able to audit what was
brought into it and on whose say-so.

schema.title: Response Source Permissions Api V1 Groups  Group Id  Sources Permissions Get

post.description:
Upload one file as a source (member+).

The file's BYTES are the request body (no multipart form): the
frontend sends the file with ``filename`` as a query parameter.
Content is sniffed, never trusted by extension (B-025).

Upload one voice note (raw body; see the file route's note).

The audio is stored, a ``voice`` source opens in
awaiting-transcription, and a transcription job is enqueued;
the response names the job so its status stays visible.

delete.description:
Delete a source (organiser+). Its chunks and provenance go
with it; anything drafted from it stays, as a tombstone.

get.description: One source with its chunks, in order (member+).

post.description:
Run the calendar return path for a Samtal source.

Out: published events appear on the hall's calendar.
In: Samtal-side edits arrive as CHANGE CANDIDATES in the
review queue — never as silent writes. The event itself
does not move until a person approves the candidate.

Ask for an extraction run over one source (B-045): a
durable job is queued (202 + its id); the candidates land in
this queue when the worker runs it.

Ask for a vision reading of one flyer/board source
(Phase 5, B-063/B-064/B-069): a durable job is queued
(202 + its id). A board is segmented and each poster read;
the drafts land in this queue when the worker runs it, and
the job's progress says how far through the posters it is.

Undelete a source inside its 30-day window (B-080): the
tombstone snapshot rebuilds it with its original ids —
chunks, provenance and flyers — and its candidates lose
their source-deleted stamps.

get.description:
A live source's speakers, resolved through account
links (member+). Unlinked speakers answer guest=True —
even when their name is a member's name. That is the
identity law, and this response is where it shows.

schema.title: Response List Speakers Api V1 Groups  Group Id  Sources  Source Id  Speakers Get

post.description:
Poll a live source's connector for new messages.

New messages land as chunks, in order, under the
permission record the source was registered with. A
connector that cannot answer — no live Samtal configured,
Messenger's ungranted access — refuses in plain words and
the refusal is recorded on the source's sync state.

get.description:
Server-sent events for the group's job-driven work.

Backed by the Job table (services/stream.py) — what a client
sees here is the durable record, never an in-memory rumour.
The group's sub-groups, name order, with headcounts.

Change my password (current password required); every
existing session is revoked by the service (B-020).

Record a provider's bounce/complaint: a bounce also
marks its notification failed, so the address shows on
the admin failure list.

Signature (B-133): when the deployment sets
GPA_MAIL_WEBHOOK_SECRET, the provider signs the raw body
(HMAC-SHA256 hex in ``x-gpa-mail-signature``) and an
unsigned or mis-signed event is refused 401 and records
NOTHING — a provider's word about an address is only
worth acting on when it is really the provider's.

The receiver: one signed delivery → chunks on its source.

The credential is the token in the path plus the
``x-gpa-signature`` HMAC over ``x-gpa-timestamp`` and the
raw body. Verification — token, window, signature,
replay receipt — happens inside services/webhooks_in.py
before a single chunk is written; refusals are logged
there too.
